title: What If Elon Musk Took the AI Race to Space?
brief:
Today's video retells the YouTube video "What If Elon Musk Took the AI Race to Space?" by Afterhour Theory (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=znWzWYHoLOg), chosen by the owner: the same story, beats and flow. Verify its names, numbers, dates and claims from other credible sources, and find the exact figures.
What that video says: You’re Elon Musk, the world’s first trillionaire, and you’re losing the AI race to a company you co-founded, OpenAI. Google and Anthropic are beating you, too, and it annoys you. But they don’t know your secret genius master plan. First, you need an AI company, so you build xAI. Now, to train your AI model, you need GPUs. So, xAI builds Colossus, one of the largest AI data centers in just 122 days. That’s just 4 months. Then, Nvidia and TSMC can’t make chips fast enough because you can’t wait and want to go at full speed. So, you announce Terafab, your own chip factory. Now, your AI is starving for training data. So, you strike a $60 billion deal for Cursor, a software company that a lot of people use to build software with AI. Then, you launch Grokbot, an AI agent company, so regular people hand it their work every day. Still not enough? You bought Twitter back in 2022. It’s a social media platform for intellectual people to post their thoughts. Every post, every reply is more data and a megaphone and promotion system for everything you sell because you control the algorithm. And you’re not even halfway. You need real-world data and images. So, you build a self-driving car company called Tesla that captures real-world data of the streets. Then, Tesla builds Optimus 3, a robot with hands gentle enough to hold an egg with fine motor control. And every move it makes is more data. Then, you hit the wall. Your AI needs three things Earth can’t give it: power, internet, cooling. So, you look at the moon. The moon has no tax, no politics, no shortage of space, and it’s a short distance away. It takes 3 days to reach the moon from Earth. So, you start a rocket company called SpaceX that builds Starship, a rocket that lands and flies again. Now, you need internet to train your AI. So, you create Starlink. You wrap the planet in your own fleet of satellites, and millions of homes, ships, and planes connect through you. And you can even build spy satellites for the US government. And you also bought a solar company called SolarCity and renamed it Tesla Energy. Your own solar company starts the biggest build anyone has ever imagined, a Dyson sphere. Picture the sun as a light bulb. Almost all its light flies off into space, wasted. Now surround it with millions of solar panels, swarming like bees, catching the light before it escapes. Up there, the sun never sets and the heat glows away into the freezing dark. Now you’ve won. But one day, the internet runs out of things to say. So you open the last company, Neuralink, a chip that reads straight from the human brain. And now you can go and expand your business to Mars, too, because you already own the Earth, like literally.
